name: Donut Chart
summary: Donut Chart. A dense, readable data primitive with semantic structure and resilient overflow.

lifecycle.compatibility: Available for controlled production evaluation; the contract may still be refined.
lifecycle.rationale: The part-to-whole primitive remains beta while legend scale, formatting, and manual assistive-technology evidence mature.
knownLimitations: The primitive is intentionally limited to one series and does not group very small segments.
Consumers must choose a different representation when segment count or similarity impairs comparison.
promotionCriteria: Public API, defaults, aliases and entrypoint ownership are reviewed.
SSR/hydration, keyboard, accessibility and visual evidence are linked.
Runtime scale limits and consumer testing contract are documented.
Migration impact is classified before lifecycle promotion.

keyboard: Tab reaches the source-data toggle and each native legend button.
Focus on a legend button reveals its matching segment and value.
Enter and Space use native button activation; SVG segments do not duplicate tab stops.
notes: Legend buttons provide the keyboard interaction surface for visual segments.
A semantic source-data table exposes the same labels and values.
Labels and values supplement color and geometry.
KERN avoids ambient browser globals in reusable runtime infrastructure.
Validate the consuming SSR/hydration route, locale, ids and overlay host.

examples.title: Typed portfolio mix donut chart

guidance.useWhen: Use Donut Chart for a small part-to-whole composition with clearly distinguishable proportions.
guidance.avoidWhen: Use Bar Chart when precise comparison matters or when many small segments would be difficult to distinguish.

commonMistakes: Importing from an undeclared family path or a source implementation file.
Loading only tokens.css instead of the complete styles/kern.css component bundle.
Assuming the documentation SSR build replaces validation of the consuming application.
Avoid Donut Chart when many segments or small differences make comparison unreliable.
checklist: Import the symbol from its documented owner entrypoint; do not use a deep source import.
Load @kern-ui/angular/styles/kern.css exactly once in the application's global styles.
Provide every required input and keep collection identities stable across updates.
Verify keyboard, focus, visible labels, invalid state, long text, RTL and 200% zoom.
Test the consuming SSR/hydration route when server rendering is enabled.
Use @kern-ui/angular/testing harnesses when a component-specific harness is available.

exclusions.reason: The public type is not a lossless scalar/literal contract and requires a typed specimen fixture.

Callback inputs require executable application code and are covered by the typed specimen fixture.
